title: Pause the automatic write-off of balances over a year old
detail: Turn off the rule that writes off balances over a year old until each balance has been checked against its filing and appeal limits. Some are still collectible. Approve yourself, in writing, any standing rule that changes a claim's date, code or balance.

title: Read the first feed reports under the place-of-service rule
detail: Since November 10, 2026 (rule version 2026-11-10.4, live at 11:14 UTC) the charge import sets place of service when it enters a charge: care management in a nursing building as 32, the monthly visit as 32, weekly visits and admissions as 31. Each feed report has a place-of-service line with counts and chart numbers, and says whether AdvancedMD stored the code that was sent. The first batch (12:39 UTC, 60 visits) entered 24 Brynwood visits at 32. Its import register had not reached the live branch by 14:32 UTC, so whether AdvancedMD kept the 32s is not read yet. Read the next three reports. Check one care-management charge in AdvancedMD by hand after the November month-end batch. Note any line the Claim Inspector holds for its place of service.

title: Engage a healthcare attorney before the visit-level audit
detail: Do this before anyone reads a chart for the coding audit. Ask your malpractice insurer or the Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service for two attorneys who handle Medicare billing reviews. Ask the attorney to direct the coding audit and any review of past visit claims. A review the attorney directs can be privileged if its results stay with the attorney. Write down the date the attorney is engaged.

title: Withdrawn: attorney-directed look at care-management records
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Withdrawn: comparison of logged minutes with hours worked
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Withdrawn: choice of code per patient from the records
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Keep each month's consent, care plan and time log where they can be pulled by patient and month
detail: The billing routine stores, with each care-management claim, a note of where that month's records are kept. No claim waits on this.

title: Find out why Medicare denies some care-management lines as the wrong provider type
detail: 38 complex-code lines since June were denied with reason 170 and remark N95. Call First Coast's provider line, or have a staff member call, and ask what triggers it and whether the place of service on the claim is part of it.

title: Check each patient's status before a care-management claim is built
detail: If the patient died, left the practice's care or elected hospice during the month, bill only when the full time was logged before that day. Never use a date of service after the date of death. Place of service now comes from the import's rule (32 for care management in a nursing building, 31 in a month the chart looks skilled); compare it with the facility's Part A list when the list arrives.

title: Write down where each kind of record is kept
detail: List visit notes, care plans, consents and care-management time logs. For each, name the system or facility that holds it and who can pull a copy. Confirm the practice can get a copy of any note when a payer asks for it.

title: Withdrawn: attorney's written advice on care-management claims already paid
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Have the attorney set, in writing, the dates that govern any refund
detail: The rule gives 60 days to report and return an overpayment once it is identified. A prompt, good-faith review of related claims pauses that deadline, for no more than 180 days after the first overpayment was identified (title 42 of the Code of Federal Regulations, section 401.305). The attorney decides when each clock starts. As an outer guide only: counted from this report, November 10, 2026, day 60 is January 9, 2027 and day 180 is May 9, 2027. Put the attorney's dates on the calendar, and send any audit finding of an overpayment to the attorney the same week.

title: Write one page on why revenue fell from 2023 to 2025
detail: List the sites, services and staff that were lost and why, and what brought revenue back in 2026. A buyer or a lender will ask, and the budget needs it.

title: Have the attorney engage a certified outside auditor
detail: Ask for experience with hospital and nursing facility visits and for both over- and under-coding findings.

title: Have the auditor draw the random sample
detail: The software gives the auditor a list of every visit claim from the last six months. The auditor picks 10 notes per code family per clinician, about 80 to 100 notes.

title: Send the notes securely
detail: Clinical notes come from the health record, not from the billing database.

title: Review the report with the attorney, then with both clinicians as the attorney advises
detail: Agree what changes in how levels are chosen and documented.

title: Schedule the quarterly 10-chart audit
detail: Same auditor, both clinicians, results logged.

title: Ask the auditor to include 10 advance care planning notes
detail: Advance care planning has a high national error rate for missing documentation of time.

title: Log each initial visit in Claimocity under the clinician who saw the patient
detail: From rule version 2026-11-10.6 (live on the billing branch November 10, 2026) billing enters every initial nursing facility visit (99306) and its advance care planning line (99497) under the physician and the group, as the owner directed that day: 'going forward the 99306 should always be billed under [the physician's] npi and group npi as i am the one who is doing the initial hps 99306 and 99497'. That is right only when he personally did the visit. Since October 28 the feed has named the nurse practitioner on 10 of 19 initial visits, so fix it at the source: whoever logs an initial visit in Claimocity logs it under the clinician who saw the patient. If the nurse practitioner does an initial visit, tell billing so it goes out under her. Past claims are not listed or reopened: the owner did not ask for it. A workbook of the 982 past initial visits under her code was given to him on November 10.

title: Write down how a visit level gets from the note to the claim, and what changed in 2024 and in 2026
detail: Do this for the attorney, after the attorney is engaged. The physician's share of top-level hospital follow-ups was 64.5% in 2023, 1.3% in 2024 and 73.7% now. For each period record who picked the code, in which tool, and whether the tool offers a default level. The attorney shares it with the auditor.

title: Add a monthly table of each clinician's level mix against the national mix to the scorecard
detail: For each code family, show the share billed at each level beside the national share.

title: Hold a coding education session built from the audit's findings
detail: Use what the attorney agrees to share from the audit. Both clinicians attend. Record the date and who was there.

title: Add a time statement and the required elements to the advance care planning note
detail: At least 16 minutes of discussion is needed to bill it. The note states the minutes, who took part and that the talk was voluntary. Those minutes are not counted toward the visit billed the same day. From January 1, 2027 code 99497 covers only time the billing clinician personally spent. Time spent by staff uses new codes G0572 and G0573.

title: Ask each of the five nursing facilities for a weekly census with payer, skilled-stay status and the start and end date of each skilled stay
detail: The business office produces this already for its own billing.

title: Store skilled-stay, hospice and plan status by date
detail: New fields on the patient record in the database.

title: Check each month's claims billed as 32 against the facility's Part A list
detail: The back end sets place of service from the visit pattern. The facility's list of residents in a Part A stay is the proof. Each month, compare the claims billed as 32 with the list and tell the owner of any resident who was in a Part A stay on the date of service. Ask First Coast in writing whether care management may be billed for a month in which the resident was in a Part A stay for part of the month. A 2016 Medicare question-and-answer sheet said no. The current one says care management can be billed for nursing facility residents and does not repeat that limit.

title: Done November 10, 2026: the past year's claims are counted
detail: From November 2025 through October 2026, 3,505 care-management lines were billed in the five nursing buildings. Medicare paid 1,667 of them, $85,176, none at the long-term rate (95.3% exactly at the skilled-stay amount). At the long-term rate the same lines would have been allowed $76,549 more: $60,015 from Medicare and $15,310 from patients or secondary payers. For visits the two codes paid differently only in 2026: 1,530 Medicare-paid visits from January to October, and at most $16,383 more Medicare payment ($20,897 allowed) if every one had been a long-term resident; most of them are the nurse practitioner's, paid at 85%. A workbook with the lines by month, code, setting, clinician and payer was given to the owner.

title: Withdrawn: asking Medicare to reopen claims billed as skilled stays
detail: Withdrawn at the owner's direction on November 10, 2026. The past year was sized at $60,015 of Medicare payment not claimed on care management. The owner decided to change new claims only and not to ask Medicare to reopen paid ones.

title: Withdrawn: past skilled-stay dates for every resident
detail: Withdrawn on November 10, 2026. Past stay dates were wanted only to size and correct past claims, and the owner decided that day to change new claims only. The monthly Part A list from each facility going forward is still wanted (see the census items).

title: Work the open coverage cards
detail: 349 of 503 cards on the Insurance Refresh Board were open on November 10, 2026. The refresh stopped in mid-September after passes by hand on September 5-8 and 23-24, and no routine works the open cards. That day 136 cards with nothing left to bill or collect were closed on the owner's word; 7 went to his turn (6 end with his own October note and no reply, 1 names a patient with no chart number), 3 stay open because money is owed on another chart of the card, and 1 stays open because its chart has no charges yet. One of the 7 holds a face sheet he pasted with the insurance the card waited for: billing enters that insurance, and no answer is needed from him. Next: the 145 charts with money waiting ($153,124; 101 seen in the last 30 days, $125,260), biggest balance and most recent first. Electronic check first, portal second, facility business office third.

title: Start the check-only coverage run on the first of each month
detail: Approved by the owner on November 10, 2026 as check-only: the run reads, records, compares with last month and writes board cards and a short report; it changes no chart, adds or ends no plan and re-sends no claim. Medicare is asked only about patients being billed that month, because Medicare does not allow checks not tied to real claims. Expected use is 40 to 70 paid checks, about $10 to $40 a month, capped at 150 checks or $75 a run with at most 25 discovery searches; a one-time catch-up costs at most about 450 checks, about $260 (estimates). Its build started on November 11, 2026, after rule version .7 went live (version .6 and the look-up savings went live on November 10); the owner creates the monthly routine on the web page from text billing gives him.

title: List every held visit daily and re-check held charts
detail: The insurance check's HOLD is a label in its report, not a stop in AdvancedMD: 56 held visits on charts with a plan were billed anyway. So a held visit can still go out with no verified payer. List every held visit each day with its reason, and re-check held charts that have no new visit: today the check runs again only when a new visit arrives, and 26 of 50 held patients were never re-checked. Making a hold stop a claim in AdvancedMD is a later change that needs the owner's word.

title: Get portal access for the Medicaid long-term care plan with $26,640 open
detail: It allows eligibility only through its portal and pays by paper check.

title: Done November 10, 2026: feed visits with no plan or no claim counted
detail: Of 1,037 visits in the first 13 feed batches (from October 28), 138 ($29,286, 13.7% of dollars) arrived with no open plan on the chart. The look-up named a payer for 76 of them, but only 7 of those were billed, because of the never-billed defect. On November 10, 122 feed visits ($26,373) had no claim: 86 with a payer on the chart that were never sent ($19,405; 84 of them the never-billed visits), 21 with no plan at all ($4,358; a face sheet is needed) and 15 moved to the patient's balance ($2,610). These are unbilled charges, not a forecast of collections. The daily never-billed list in rule version .7 keeps the count current.

title: Compare each day's visits by site with the charges entered, and list the gaps
detail: A visit on the census with no charge goes on a short daily list.

title: Sort the correct-and-resend list by each payer's filing deadline
detail: Medicare: one year from the date of service. Florida Medicaid plans: six months from the date of service when the plan pays first. When Medicare pays first, the state's plan contract allows three years from the date of service. When another insurer pays first, 90 days from that insurer's final decision. Ask each plan which of these it applies when a Medicare Advantage plan pays first. Florida Medicaid itself, after Medicare: 12 months from the date of service or six months after Medicare's decision, whichever is later. Other plans: the contract. Check each plan's provider manual before treating any claim as too late. These limits are for sending a claim the first time. A Medicare claim that was denied is usually fixed by a reopening request within one year of the decision or an appeal within 120 days of it. Only a claim Medicare returned as incomplete is sent again.

title: Work the 74 actionable denials worth $13,463
detail: From the latest billing run. Leave out any fix that changes a code, a date, a modifier, a diagnosis or the place of service until a person has approved it.

title: Dispute recent denials coded as not payable under a managed care contract
detail: 32 recent lines carry this code: 21 top-level hospital follow-ups, plus hospital and nursing facility admissions. First find which plan sent each one, whether the practice is in that plan's network, and whether the denial is still inside the plan's dispute window.

title: Report receivables by age and payer every Monday
detail: One table on the dashboard.

title: Report denials by cause and payer each month
detail: One table on the dashboard. Pick one cause to fix each month.

title: File the physician's Florida Medicaid provider agreement renewal
detail: The agreement expires December 27, 2026 (the agency's letter of September 29, 2026). File by November 13, this item's date. December 1 is the last call the practice set, to leave the agency time to process it; Thanksgiving week and Christmas week leave few working days, and December 27 is a Sunday. Reset the Florida Medicaid portal password first: it expired November 4 unless it was changed, and the renewal is filed in that portal. Ask for written confirmation that the renewal is complete, not only received. Use the nurse practitioner's returned application to see what the agency rejects.

title: Resubmit the nurse practitioner's new Florida Medicaid application
detail: It is a new application, not a revalidation: her old Medicaid number ended. The agency returned it with three faults: the provider agreement form (December 2023 version, every page signed and dated), her Level 2 background screening, and the collaborating physician named exactly as on the signed collaborative agreement. She signs it. Then call Provider Enrollment to confirm receipt and ask for an effective date back to the day her old number ended.

title: Correct the nurse practitioner's national provider record
detail: Current address and the right specialty code.

title: Stop writing off Railroad Medicare claims and ask about any it refused
detail: Railroad Medicare is paying: it paid $718.76 in 2026 and $3,764 is open, and its numbers are on the credentialing board. The plan's earlier 'not enrolled' looks wrong for the group and the physician. Whether the nurse practitioner has a Railroad Medicare number is not known. Stop writing off these claims. Have a person ask Palmetto GBA, the Railroad Medicare contractor, about any claim it refused and why, whether the nurse practitioner has a number, and how to get her one if she has none. A claim may be filed up to one year after the date of service.

title: Resolve the terminated commercial plan
detail: Confirm in writing whether the physician is participating, and re-apply if not. First read Cigna's three secure messages of September 9: they can be opened only until 7:30 AM Eastern on Tuesday December 8, so the last day is Monday December 7. Do not ask for a specialty change.

title: Finish Veterans Affairs portal registration, and ask TRICARE East about the nurse practitioner
detail: The nurse practitioner signs her own applications. The software can prepare the forms. TRICARE East's electronic claims and remittance enrollment was approved in October 2026; whether it will take the nurse practitioner into its network is still to be asked, and its portal sign-in is cleared only by phone.

title: Build one expiry calendar for both clinicians
detail: Licenses, registrations, board certification, privileges, every payer enrollment, and the nurse practitioner's protocol (or autonomous practice registration) with its date. Include each clinician's re-attestation date for the shared credentialing profile (CAQH), which lapses after 120 days, and each Medicare revalidation due date from Medicare's revalidation list: a missed revalidation means unpaid visits from the due date. Use the existing sheet 'Practice compliance & renewals calendar', which mirrors to Google Calendar. On November 10, 2026, 22 rows were added (quality program and credentialing) and 34 calendar entries were made. One of the new rows is the physician's board-certification yearly assessment, due November 30, 2026; it is not known whether it is done. The sheet is rebuilt by a weekly routine whose November 9 run did not finish. Check on Monday November 16 that it kept the 22 new rows and doubled nothing. The sheet's routine makes only a 14-day warning, so the 90-day warnings must be added by hand.

title: Close the open items on the hospital reappointment
detail: Call the medical staff office this week. Ask for the list of what is missing and the date the current appointment ends, then send everything. The hospital is 37.8% of charges.

title: UnitedHealthcare: the network removal notice, and the next directory attestation about November 26
detail: The directory attestation is not overdue: it was done August 28, 2026 and is next due about November 26, which is Thanksgiving, so do it by November 25. The open UnitedHealthcare matter is a network removal notice whose first pages (which network, the reason and the dates) are missing: call about it. UnitedHealthcare and its plan for people with Medicare and Medicaid hold $48,140 of open receivables.

title: Complete the last two required courses for the Sunshine plan
detail: Two of the eight required courses are left (credentialing board, November 10, 2026). Only one practice representative needs to complete them. Ask the plan which clinician it lists as overdue, and keep the completion record.

title: Fix TRICARE For Life's rejected electronic enrollment, and get an authorization number before each Veterans Affairs visit is billed
detail: TRICARE East's electronic claims (approved October 9, 2026) and remittances (October 5) are approved. TRICARE For Life's claims agreement was denied September 30 and its remittance agreement October 21 ('provider is not set up at payor - invalid trading partner ID'). Ask AdvancedMD's enrollment desk which trading partner ID the payer expects, resubmit both and get written confirmation. Do not send a Veterans Affairs claim until its authorization number is on it.

title: Explain the $12,902 of Medicare deposits with no remittance
detail: Find and post the remittances.

title: Chase the large plan whose remittances arrived with no money
detail: Call the plan this week. Ask how each payment since August was sent. If it was sent as a one-time card number, ask for it to be reissued and switch to bank deposit. The software lists the remittances that have no matching deposit.

title: Complete electronic remittance and deposit enrollment for every payer
detail: Including the plan whose enrollment was rejected. The software prepares each form. The owner signs it and confirms the bank account.

title: Have the accountant reconcile the bank account monthly
detail: Someone other than the person, or the software, that posts payments.

title: Re-authorize the accounting software connection
detail: So monthly results can load into the practice database.

title: Agree a monthly close by the 15th with the accountant
detail: Income statement, balance sheet and a cash summary.

title: Build the 2027 budget with four scenarios
detail: Steady, loss of the largest site, a second nurse practitioner, and care-management collections falling by half. Price the 2027 Medicare changes code by code, not as a flat 2.31% cut: hospital visits fall 3% to 5% and nursing facility visits billed as a skilled stay rise 10% to 12%.

title: Hold the first monthly review
detail: Scorecard, work list, cash, and one decision recorded.

title: Done November 10, 2026: payments, adjustments and write-offs by month of service are in the database
detail: The full AdvancedMD history is in the practice database: 11,050 charts; 84,617 charge lines (68,727 live), 91,094 payment lines and 108,768 write-off lines, dates of service 2022 to November 2026, checked as an exact copy. Its table definitions were corrected the same day. Read money by year of service: AdvancedMD's payment date is the day a payment was entered. Posted payments for 2022 to 2025 are a floor: 12,821 charge lines with $1,910,279.88 of fees were closed in May 2026 as 'paid, not posted', so up to about $1.0 million more may have been received. Next: compute the net collection rate by month of service, with 2022 to 2025 labelled 'posted payments'.

title: Name one person to keep this work list
detail: A staff member or an outside project manager keeps the list, chases each item and reports to you each week. Until mid-December keep for yourself only what needs your judgment or signature: engaging the attorney, signing the Medicaid renewal, and approving any billing rule that changes a claim's date, code or balance. Hand the facility calls, the plan portal access and the accounting link to that person or to the nurse practitioner. Leave the database key change with whoever already administers the database.

title: Write a compliance program of a few pages with the attorney
detail: The seven elements from federal guidance, scaled down.

title: Collect every medical director agreement from the past six years, with fair-market-value support and time logs
detail: For the attorney's review. Two are active in 2026. Five or more were active in 2023, when stipends were $185,300. Stipends were $54,000 in 2024 and $96,500 in 2025. Include agreements that have ended, with the end date and the reason. Start a monthly time log for the two active ones now.

title: Do a security risk analysis
detail: Assess the risks to all electronic patient information the practice holds: where it is stored and sent, who and what can reach it (including the software agents and their keys), what could go wrong, how likely and how serious it is, and what will be done about each risk. Include the vendor list, each business associate agreement and where each vendor stores data. Have someone other than the billing agent review and sign it. The free federal Security Risk Assessment Tool at healthit.gov is built for small practices. The owner signs and dates the result.

title: Have the auditor read the billing rulebook's high-risk rules
detail: Any rule that changes a code, date, modifier, diagnosis, place of service or balance, except the rules for care-management claims. The owner confirmed on November 10, 2026 that consent, care plans and time records are on file for these claims.

title: Name one person to receive record requests and log deadlines
detail: Pick the person who opens the mail and the payer portals each business day. Log each request the day it arrives: who sent it, which claims, the due date and what was sent back.

title: Add a required-visit due date for every nursing facility resident
detail: Every 30 days for the first 90 days, then every 60 days, each with 10 days of grace. Record who must make each visit: in a Medicare Part A skilled stay the physician makes the first visit and at least every other required visit. For other residents Florida's rule allows another licensed professional. Ask the attorney whether that covers the first visit.

title: Get a written statement of where each vendor stores patient information
detail: Florida requires patient information kept offsite or in the cloud to stay in the continental United States, its territories or Canada. Ask every software and AI vendor.

title: Record yearly compliance training for both clinicians
detail: One hour is enough. Keep the date, the topics and the names.

title: Have the attorney read the nurse practitioner's employment agreement and her Florida practice protocol
detail: Florida requires a written protocol kept at each place she practices, unless she is registered for autonomous practice.

title: Check that every Advance Beneficiary Notice form is the current version
detail: Since May 12, 2026 only the form marked 'Exp. 03/31/2029' is valid for Original Medicare. Check the templates in the record system, any paper copies each clinician carries and any packets a facility supplies. The notice is required when Medicare is likely to deny a service as not medically necessary, such as a wellness visit repeated too soon. An old form on such a denial can leave the write-off with the practice. Raised by the vendor's newsletter and checked against Medicare's own announcement.

title: Turn off open sign-up on this application
detail: A check added on November 10, 2026 refuses any account whose address has not been confirmed. Before that, an account needed only an approved address. Read the access log for sign-ins nobody recognizes, confirm that the approved address's account belongs to its owner, and write down what was found. Then turn off open sign-up. The access log was read on November 10, 2026: 31 requests, all on November 7, all from the one confirmed account, and none refused. Only one account exists.

title: Replace the database access key that was pasted into a chat
detail: Revoke it in the database console today and issue a new one. Then read the database's connection and query logs for the days the key was exposed, and write down what was found and what was done. If the console shows no logs, ask the database vendor for them. If the logs show access nobody can explain, tell the attorney, because the breach notification rules may apply.

title: Require the owner's written approval for any rule that changes a claim's code, date, modifier, diagnosis, place of service or balance
detail: The software builds the check and lists the rules. You approve each one in writing before it runs.

title: Sample 25 automated actions each month and record the result
detail: The correction rate becomes a scorecard measure.

title: Make every write-off carry a reason code, and keep patient balances out of the automatic rule
detail: Routine waiver of Medicare copayments and deductibles is unlawful, and billing a Qualified Medicare Beneficiary for them is forbidden. The automatic rule should touch insurance balances only. A patient balance is written off only with a reason: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary, documented hardship, or unpaid after documented attempts to collect.

title: Run a credit balance report, and confirm the November 2 write-off touched only amounts owed to the practice
detail: List every account where a payer or patient is owed money. Check that none of the $40,686 written off was a credit. The owner reviews the list.

title: Done November 10, 2026: both clinicians looked up in the participation status tool
detail: Both must take part in 2026 and both are in a small practice, so the electronic-records category is dropped. Neither has disaster relief for 2025 or 2026. The physician was scored on the hospital's results for 2025 and is not for 2026: the hospital share of his Medicare lines fell from 95% to 64% in the measuring periods.

title: Done November 10, 2026: 2025 feedback and payment adjustment read
detail: Physician: 65.81 points, a 1.10% cut from January 1, 2027. Quality 82.94 and cost 75.43 came from the hospital's scores, improvement activities scored zero, and a 10-point bonus for complex patients was added. Nurse practitioner: 16.31 points, a 9% cut. Nothing was reported, the cost score was 54.35, and the 10-point bonus was not added because nothing was submitted. The request for a review of the 2025 result closes November 30, 2026 at 8 p.m. Eastern; not having reported is not a ground for one.

title: Done November 10, 2026: group and both clinicians registered for the neurological option
detail: Decided November 10, 2026: the advance care plan code goes on the next Medicare claim of every patient 65 or older, once per patient; depression screening was not chosen. The code states that a plan or a named decision-maker is documented in each coded patient's record, and it rests on the owner's 'yes for all' (see the work item on the code). Value in Primary Care, the first choice, has four claim measures, so one measure fills a quarter of its quality score. Quality Care for Patients with Neurological Conditions (M0004) has one claim measure, the advance care plan, so the same codes fill 90%. The group, the physician and the nurse practitioner are each registered for M0004 (the owner pasted the three registration screens on November 10; each shows status Complete). The compliance sheet has a row to save a copy of each as proof by November 30, 2026, when edits close at 8 p.m. Eastern. CMS lists this option for neurology and for nurse practitioners and has no rule limiting the choice; whether CMS would question it for a nursing-facility practice is the open point, and the service center (1-866-288-8292) can say.

title: Attest the improvement activity for 2026
detail: Between January 4 and March 31, 2027 (8 p.m. Eastern), at qpp.cms.gov: Start Reporting, Report as a Group, then under Improvement Activities create a manual entry, enter the dates and tick the activity as completed. Do it under the registered reporting option with an activity from that option's list (neurological option: advance care planning, medication management, fall screening) and under traditional reporting, and again for each clinician: six entries in all. The activity must have run 90 days in a row in 2026, so it must have been running by October 3, 2026. At least half of the clinicians billing under the tax number must have carried it out. A calendar entry is set for Monday January 4, 2027 at 9:00 AM. The CMS sign-in password must be changed every 60 days; the one set on November 10 lapses about January 9, 2027, in the first attestation week. Check the lookup in December first: if CMS grants automatic disaster relief for 2026, a group submission cancels it.

title: List long-term residents with no wellness visit in the last 12 months
detail: Use the census and the billing history. Mark any resident whose last wellness visit date is not known.

title: Schedule wellness visits, about a dozen a month
detail: Work from the list, one facility at a time.

title: Set up a transitional care routine for discharges to assisted living or home
detail: Contact within two business days and a visit within 7 or 14 days.

title: Reset the fee schedule each January
detail: Every charge above the highest contracted rate. This needs the contract rates, which are due by the end of February. The software drafts the schedule and the owner approves it.

title: Request the current contract and fee schedule from every plan
detail: Write to each plan's provider relations office. Ask for the signed contract, every amendment and the current fee schedule for the practice's codes.

title: Load the 2027 Medicare fee schedule for the practice's locality
detail: Medicare published the 2027 values in November 2026. First Coast posts the fees for each Florida area in its Fee Schedule Lookup.

title: Reprice the top 15 codes at 2027 rates by site of service
detail: Show the change per code and in total.

title: Flag any payment below the expected amount
detail: Compare each paid line with the loaded fee schedule and list the differences each week.

title: Confirm 2027 network status with each Medicare Advantage plan
detail: Plans set their 2027 networks and benefits in mid-2026, and Medicare published the 2027 star ratings on October 8, 2026. Ask each plan in writing whether both clinicians stay in network for 2027. Look up each plan's rating on Medicare's plan finder: a plan under 4 stars loses a bonus and a plan under 3.5 gets a smaller rebate share, and those plans tend to tighten authorization and payment. Raised by the vendor's newsletter and checked against Medicare's rules.

title: Get two refinance quotes for the $187,206 note
detail: Check the note for a prepayment charge first.

title: Agree a plan to retire the $162,121 owed by the owner
detail: Repayment, pay or distribution, and the tax effect of each.

title: Review the owner's salary against market pay
detail: Reasonable compensation for an S corporation owner.

title: Set a cash floor and start a 13-week cash forecast
detail: A cash floor is the lowest bank balance you allow before owner draws pause. Ninety days of spending is about $177,000, and cash was $94,431 on September 30, 2026. Agree with the accountant what owner distributions are paid until the floor is reached. A 13-week forecast is one row a week of expected deposits and payments. Ask the accountant for a template.

title: Ask the broker about cyber and billing-audit defense cover
detail: Call the malpractice insurer and the insurance broker this week. Ask whether the current policy pays for the defense of a billing audit, and whether it requires an attorney from the insurer's list. Ask only what the policy covers. Leave any description of the reviews to the attorney.

title: Tell the accountant about any personal tax balance, and include it when asking for loan quotes
detail: Any personal tax balance owed to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and any payment plan on it, is outside the practice. It still bears on distributions, on any refinance and on a sale.

title: Ask the bank for a line of credit
detail: The risk review lists an unused line of credit as a control. Ask while 2026 results are strong.

title: Write a two-page emergency plan
detail: Who covers patients, who can sign, who has access to bank and systems, and who can pause the billing software if you are away. Add who would tell patients and facilities, and who would keep the records, if the practice had to stop.

title: Sign a mutual coverage agreement with another physician
detail: Ask a physician who already sees patients at the same hospital or facilities. Put in writing who covers whom, for how long and how each is paid.

title: Start a relationship record for each site
detail: Decision makers, last contact, what they want, any agreement and its end date.

title: Review disability, key-person and business overhead insurance
detail: Ask the insurance broker what each policy would pay if you could not work for three months.

title: Introduce the nurse practitioner to the administrator at each site
detail: Start with the three largest sites.

title: List every nursing and assisted living facility within 40 minutes
detail: Beds, current physician coverage and a contact.

title: Build the hiring case
detail: Six-month ramp, three-month enrollment delay, cost and break-even census.

title: Decide, and if yes start enrollment the day the offer is signed
detail: Use the hiring case. Decide only after the coding audit is finished.

title: Open a data room folder with the standard sections
detail: Financial, contracts, billing reports, compliance, people, systems.

title: Separate recurring collections from recovery of old receivables each month
detail: Use dates of service from the AdvancedMD history now in the practice database, and deposit dates from the bank. AdvancedMD's payment date is the day a payment was entered, not the day it arrived: all-payer payments dated 2025 total only $2,812.68. Do not rely on the valuation until this is done.

title: Choose a target year for stepping back
detail: Plan three to five years ahead.

title: Refresh the valuation with a full year of clean numbers
detail: Use twelve months of monthly statements and the split of recurring and one-time collections.

title: Answer three questions the place-of-service rule cannot answer from the chart
detail: One: when a long-term resident comes back from the hospital on skilled days, is the first visit back always billed as an initial visit? If it is sometimes billed as a follow-up, the rule can read it as the monthly visit and bill 32. Two: a monthly resident gets one extra sick visit. The rule bills that visit as 31 and keeps that month's care management at 31. Should both be 32? Three: the safeguard that leaves care management at 31 in a month with a hospital visit, a home or assisted living visit, an admission or weekly visits: keep it or remove it? Each such line is listed in the feed report and goes out at 31 unless changed first.

title: Mark which of the 148 October visits were the physician's own
detail: The list gives chart, visit, date and codes for each visit the feed names the nurse practitioner on that was entered under the physician. Start with the 4 initial visits: on November 10 the owner said 'i saw those patients' about the 2 of them that were never billed, so those stay under him. Any visit the physician performed himself is right as it stands. The question behind it: is the clinician on a Claimocity charge always the person who saw the patient?

title: Correct the clinician on the October visits that were the nurse practitioner's
detail: Decided November 10, 2026 for the 15 lines not yet billed (12 of the 84 never-billed feed visits): the 10 visits that are not initial visits move to the nurse practitioner before they are sent, and the 2 initial visits stay under the physician. A billing chat session makes the moves after the first save of the never-billed remedy reads back; moving a visit voids and re-enters its charges. Not decided: the 133 lines billed and not yet paid (120 of them at Medicare) and the 19 paid lines. For those the choices are a corrected claim, or for a paid line a corrected claim or a refund of the difference. Medicare pays a nurse practitioner's visit at 85% of the physician amount. Nothing else is changed until the owner says so.

title: Run the clinician check on entered visits every month
detail: tools/feed/feed_clinician_audit.py compares every visit the import entered with the clinician its feed message names. Run it on the first of each month and report any difference. It does not list initial visits entered under the physician by the owner's rule: it only counts them, and the feed report names each one. The feed report also names any visit the import could not match to its own message.

title: Never-billed fix (rule version 2026-11-10.7) and its daily list: delivered November 11, 2026; read back the first live batch
detail: The fix checks the insurance-order list after every save, never saves a billed visit when it repairs a never-billed one, reads the admission date before and after a save, words a hold by what the list shows, and adds a daily read-only list of feed visits that were never billed. It passed three independent reviews, a fix round and a re-check, which said deliver. It was delivered, merged with version .6 and the look-up savings, at 01:20 UTC on November 11, 2026; all ten of the billing self-tests passed on the delivered version. Still to do: read back the first live batch under it. The insurance check's HOLD stays a label in its report; making a hold stop a claim in AdvancedMD is a later change that needs the owner's word.

title: Done November 10, 2026: M0004 is in AdvancedMD's code list
detail: Read from AdvancedMD at 10:24 UTC on November 10: M0004 is on the procedure list as 'QUAL CARE NEUROLOGIC CND MVP'. Nothing has to be added by hand. Billing puts it once on one Medicare claim for each clinician, on a visit that also carries the advance care plan code, after the first such line is seen billed (rule version 2026-11-10.6, live at 22:46 UTC). AdvancedMD's list does not have 1124F, the code for a patient who declined to name anyone or to give a plan.

title: Advance care plan code on Medicare claims through December 31
detail: Live on the billing branch since 22:46 UTC on November 10, 2026 (rule version 2026-11-10.6), from the next feed import. The import adds one no-charge line with 1123F to the next Medicare visit of each patient 65 or older, once a year, under the visit's own clinician, and never on a hospital visit in 2026. It adds the code only to visits dated in 2026 (see the item on 2027). The code says that an advance care plan or a named decision-maker is documented in the patient's record. Asked on November 10, 2026 whether this holds for every patient the practice follows, the owner answered 'yes for all', so the statement on each claim is his, and CMS can ask for the record of any coded patient. A patient who declined needs code 1124F, which is not in AdvancedMD's code list, and one with whom it was never discussed needs 1123F with modifier 8P. A person enters both, and the owner names those patients. It starts with up to three lines and adds no more until AdvancedMD shows one of them billed; then up to 10 a run until Medicare's first answer on such a line is seen, then every eligible visit. If AdvancedMD leaves a $0.00 line off the claim, the import switches to one cent. A visit held only because of its no-charge line has that line taken off and goes out (the owner: 'doesnt appear to have any significance whiever way to just deal with it'). For the 2026 score the number of coded lines does not matter: at least one counted line and M0004 once for each clinician are what count, on claims processed by March 1, 2027. The code switches itself off in some cases, for example when AdvancedMD keeps leaving the line off the claim or a held visit's line cannot be taken off, and it stays off until the owner restarts it. Read the quality line of every feed report through December 31. From December 1 the report puts at its top any clinician with no M0004 line billed or waiting. Read the first remittances for Medicare's answer on the line.

title: Name the improvement activity and build its proof file
detail: First the owner names the one activity both clinicians carried out for 90 days in a row in 2026; it must have been running by October 3, 2026. CMS asks for no documents at attestation but can ask for them for six years. For the care-management activity it lists: a dated list of high-risk patients and either their personal care plans or evidence that care managers follow them. Gather 2026 records that show the activity ran at least 90 days in a row for both clinicians: each is attested alone as well as in the group, and both doing it covers the group rule whichever clinicians CMS counts.

title: Decide on an exception application by December 31
detail: The application is for rare events outside the practice's control that kept it from collecting or reporting. For the October 2026 hurricane the federal health department declared a public health emergency for all of Florida from October 6, and FEMA declared an emergency that included Leon County; FEMA's later major-disaster declaration does not list the county, and CMS has used only those lists for automatic relief, so none is expected. Apply only if the storm truly kept the practice from collecting data or disturbed its costs; CMS weighs how long. If it is approved for all four categories and nothing is submitted, the score is 75 and there is no cut. Data submitted later for a category cancels the relief for that category.

title: Set up 2027 before January 1
detail: Billing adds the quality code only to visits dated in 2026. From January 1, 2027 it adds none until the owner renews the rule, and in January the feed report says so at the top. So before January the owner says whether to renew it for 2027, and settles three choices that come with it: whether hospital visits are coded, whether charts where Medicare is the second payer are coded, and whether the code goes on once per patient or once for each clinician. A calendar entry for this is set for Monday December 21, 2026 at 9:00 AM. After the renewal, billing checks each month how many patients are coded. Name one improvement activity in January and file its proof as the year goes. Registration for 2027 opens April 1 and closes November 30, 2027; the attestation for 2027 is expected by March 31, 2028 (CMS has not published that window). The November 10 reminders hold the 2026 dates; billing adds the 2027 ones as CMS publishes them.

title: Agree a price with the look-up vendor only on written per-check rates
detail: The look-up vendor, Stedi, billed $1,879.97 for September 5-30 and $2,029.25 for October 2026 at its public prices. October: claim status 6,770 checks $889.50 (44%), Medicare-number look-ups 1,064 $783.50 (39%), insurance discovery 187 $237.00, eligibility checks 505 $113.25. On October 30 it offered to take the bill 'from almost $2k to just above $1.3k' a month on a custom plan, with no rates, minimum, term or payment method stated. October is a poor baseline: a one-time claim-status sweep (3,826 checks, 2,948 of them on 21 claims asked 31 to 164 times) ended November 2. Without it October was about $1,372 to $1,619 at public prices, and after the practice's own changes an October-size month is about $450 to $975 (estimates). So a $1,300 monthly commitment could cost more than paying as you go. A reply went on November 10 (12:30 UTC) asking for the price of each kind of check, any minimum and term, what happens to unused amounts, the payment method, the start date and the plain Medicare price, with the expected volumes, and asking for a new Slack invitation; it commits to nothing. Check for the answer on November 11. Only the owner can click Accept on the new Slack invitation.

title: Look-up savings live: watch the first runs, and replace the installed look-up skill file
detail: Live on the billing branch since 23:44 UTC on November 10, 2026, after three independent reviews and three fix rounds. Three changes that need no contract: plain Medicare eligibility checks with the Medicare number on the chart first ($0.15, instead of a look-up at $0.40 to $1.00; the practice's Medicare enrollment at the vendor is live for the group number), one shared Medicare answer per patient per month for the pre-claim check and the deceased-patient guard, and claim status asked by need, at most once a week per claim, with caps of 150 checks or $25 a run and 400 checks or $100 a month. Still to do: watch the first nightly run and the usage log; the owner replaces his installed copy of the look-up skill with the new file billing sent him, because a push does not change it; the next statement shows the price of a plain Medicare check. Three effects of the claim-status change to put to the owner: a claim more than a year old gets no status check (kept, in line with his write-off rule of November 2); claims that stop being asked go to a hand-off list that needs a person, about 129 claims in an October-size month (estimate); and claim status is switched off for TRICARE (80 unpaid visits, $4,226) until the vendor says whether an enrollment fixes it.

title: Send the 84 never-billed feed visits as the owner approved
detail: The never-billed fix (rule version .7) has been live since November 11, 2026, so a billing session with write access to AdvancedMD can send them: one pilot visit first, read back, then the rest oldest first. Approved by the owner on November 10, 2026: the 71 visits whose payer only the look-up found go out only when an eligibility check dated to the service date shows the plan active (the checks cost about $10 to $25); the chart with two plans goes to the plan that check shows active; the 13 visits whose plan came from the feed, a face sheet or by hand are sent. The nurse practitioner's 10 visits are moved to her first; the 2 initial visits stay under the physician. A standing word lets a routine save such a visit again once its first plan lands, after read-backs of the clinician, the admission date and the insurance order, never on a billed visit. None is billed yet.
